title: Demo workshop — Delta Lake basics
intro: Demo content used when no guide files are synced yet. You build a small `customers_delta` table for RetailHub, update it with `MERGE`, look back in time and tidy the files. Pick the SQL or the PySpark track; every exercise is checked here in the guide. Running the code in the notebook is optional.

steps.title: Create the Delta table
steps.explain: A Delta table is a folder of Parquet files plus a transaction log (`_delta_log`). In Unity Catalog you create it with plain SQL. Fill in the table name and the table format.
steps.expected: `customers_delta` exists in your `silver` schema with 4 columns and 0 rows.
hints: The step title and the expected result both name the table.
Databricks uses Delta by default, but the workshop writes the format explicitly after `USING`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS silver.customers_delta (
  customer_id INT,
  name        STRING,
  city        STRING,
  updated_at  TIMESTAMP
) USING DELTA
```

steps.title: Load the first customers
steps.explain: Append the customers from the Bronze table to the new Delta table.
hints: You add rows to a table that already exists.

sql.template:
{{b1}} INTO silver.customers_delta
SELECT customer_id, name, city, updated_at
{{b2}} bronze.customers
hints: You add rows to a table that already exists.
`INSERT INTO <table> SELECT ... FROM <source>` appends the rows of a query.

```sql
INSERT INTO silver.customers_delta
SELECT customer_id, name, city, updated_at
FROM bronze.customers
```
sql.explain_extra: `INSERT INTO` adds rows; it never removes existing ones.

hints: You add rows to a table that already exists.
The writer method that targets a Unity Catalog table name is `saveAsTable`.

```python
(spark.table("bronze.customers")
   .select("customer_id", "name", "city", "updated_at")
   .write
   .mode("append")
   .saveAsTable("silver.customers_delta"))
```
pyspark.explain_extra: `mode("append")` adds rows; it never removes existing ones.

steps.title: Match Delta Lake concepts
steps.explain: Before you change data, name the parts of Delta Lake you will use in this workshop. Drag each term onto its description, or select a term and then a description.

pairs.right: Folder of JSON commits that records every change to the table
Updates matching rows and inserts new ones in one statement
Reads the table as it was at an earlier commit
Compacts many small files into fewer large ones
Deletes data files no longer referenced by the table

hints: Two of the terms read old or unused data; two change how files are stored.
Time travel uses `VERSION AS OF`; `VACUUM` is the one that can break time travel.
_delta_log → commit log; MERGE INTO → upsert; VERSION AS OF → earlier version; OPTIMIZE → compaction; VACUUM → removes unreferenced files.

steps.title: Build the MERGE statement
steps.explain: New and changed customers arrive in `bronze.customers_updates`. Put the clauses of the `MERGE` in the right order. Two blocks do not belong in a `MERGE`.
hints: A MERGE reads like a sentence: target, source, join condition, then what to do.
`ON` comes before any `WHEN`; `WHEN MATCHED` usually comes first.

```sql
MERGE INTO silver.customers_delta AS t
USING bronze.customers_updates AS s
ON t.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *
```

pyspark.note: `MERGE` is SQL in both tracks: in PySpark you run it with `spark.sql(...)`.

steps.title: Time travel query
steps.explain: Every commit creates a new table version. Arrange the blocks into a query that counts the rows before the MERGE (version 1).
hints: The version goes right after the table name, not in a `WHERE` clause.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_before_merge
FROM silver.customers_delta
VERSION AS OF 1
```

steps.title: Read the table history
steps.explain: `DESCRIBE HISTORY` lists every commit with its version, timestamp and operation.
steps.expected: At least 3 versions; the newest operation is `MERGE`.
hints: The history is a table of commits, newest first.
The command starts like the one that shows a table's columns.

```sql
DESCRIBE HISTORY silver.customers_delta
```

steps.title: Compact small files
steps.explain: Many appends leave many small files. Run `OPTIMIZE` on `customers_delta` and Z-order it by `city`, the column most filters use.
steps.expected: `DESCRIBE HISTORY` shows an `OPTIMIZE` operation as the newest version.
steps.starter: -- Compact silver.customers_delta and co-locate rows by city
hints: The command is `OPTIMIZE <table>`; Z-ordering is an extra clause.

```sql
OPTIMIZE silver.customers_delta ZORDER BY (city)
```

steps.title: Match write modes
steps.explain: Each track has its own way to say what happens to the rows already in the table.

pairs.right: Adds the rows of a query to the table
Replaces the table's rows with the rows of a query
Updates matching rows and inserts new ones
Adds the DataFrame rows to the table
Replaces the table's rows with the DataFrame
Fails when the table already exists
